svg.text: The Source You Cannot Turn Off
Whenever light hits the array, the DC side is energized.
Opening the DC disconnect stops current flow only — full string Voc still sits on every conductor upstream.
DC arc faults — solar's signature hazard
DC has no zero-crossing to snuff an arc — a
chafed conductor can sustain plasma and ignite.
"reset until it stays on" is forbidden
tests every wake-up — refuse to start below threshold.
Fault clears by noon = moisture in a connector
or J-box, dew-wet at dawn, dry by lunch.
Hunt: isolate strings at combiner, megger each, split-half to the wet connector.
Working the DC side — consolidated rules

g.text: 1. Gloves + eye protection minimum; arc-rated where thresholds demand.
2. Never open a connector under load — draw current = arc. Verify zero current first.
3. Respect fuse ratings in combiners — a string fuse is not a service disconnect.
4. Label literacy: placards map what is energized from where.

svg.text: The trade's summary: the roof is a generator that sunrise turns on, whether or not anyone is ready.
Isolate, then treat everything array-side as live, always — plan work for dawn/dusk windows or opaque coverings when a truly dead module is required.
